text: Which qualities in a woman actually matter most? Ask a woman what a man should bring to the table and she can name 10, 20, maybe 30 things. Earn this much, be this tall, be confident, be ambitious, provide, protect, lead. Their entire accounts build on telling women they are the prize who deserves the best. You've seen the videos. How much a man should earn, the bare minimum for men. Fine, good for women, actually. But ask a man the same question, what should a woman bring to the table? Most men can't even name five things. Sometimes guys ask me straight up, what qualities should I actually look for? Other times I just see it in guys' stories. The cheating, the disrespect, the drama. And almost every time it started the same way. No standards from the beginning. Because a lot of men don't actually know what they're looking for. They don't really care who's next to them as long as she's attractive and gives them attention. And then they're shocked when it all turns into chaos. Guys, if you don't define what you require, you accept whatever shows up. So today, let me give you five qualities a woman should bring to the table if you actually want a good, healthy relationship. And before anyone clips this, yes, this works both ways. Everything I'm about to say, women should expect from a man too. Hold that thought, I'll come back to it. Number one, loyalty. If you've watched the relationship stories I cover on this channel, you already know how big this one is. So let me keep it simple. Cheating is unacceptable. If she cheats on you, she's no longer your woman. Loyalty isn't a bonus, it's the baseline. Number two, care. When you're sick, stressed, overwhelmed, does she care? Or does she make it about herself? Does she ask, how are you doing? Does she try to help when you actually need it? Or does she disappear the moment things stop being fun? A woman who can't show up in your low moments shouldn't be next to you in your good ones. Number three, ability to compromise. A relationship isn't my way or nothing. If you always adjust, if you always sacrifice, if you always adapt, and she never bends, that's not a good relationship. That's imbalance. Compromise goes both ways. If she expects flexibility from you but gives none back, you don't need that. Number four, support. If you're building something, a career, a business, a future, does she support you? Is she grateful for the work and the sacrifices? Or does she compare you to other men? Why can't you be like my friend's boyfriend? Why can't you earn more? Why can't we travel every month? Why, why, why? A woman who doesn't support you while you're building isn't building with you. And number five, respect. This one is the foundation. If she disrespects you in public, if she lets her friends mock you, if she talks down about you behind your back, it is over. Because without respect, attraction dies. Without respect, loyalty dies. Without respect, everything else collapses. Now, back to what I mentioned before. This works both ways. Loyalty, care, compromise, support, respect. And men should bring all of this to the table too. This was never about women owing something to men. It's about both people knowing what actually matters before they commit. Standards aren't a weapon. They are a filter. So guys, have standards. Don't be afraid to know them, say them, and hold them. Understand that you deserve more than, oh, she's attractive and she takes me back. Define what you want, then go find the woman who actually meets it.
